item.title: Hundreds of Lime e-bikes were dumped across the pathways surrounding a junction on the evening of 31 July, making it extremely difficult and unsafe for pedestrians to pass. By the next day the bikes had gone, but this is not a case of a couple of bikes parked poorly. It was a large-scale obstruction affecting the entire junction area., 13th August
item.description:
The sheer volume of bikes left blocking the pavement at this junction was a serious safety hazard for pedestrians. This level of obstruction is far beyond isolated bad parking. It points to a failure by Lime to manage rebalancing and enforce proper parking in this area. As a regular Lime user myself, I have no issue with the service in principle, but this kind of irresponsible, large-scale dumping of bikes on pedestrian infrastructure is unacceptable. I have video evidence documenting the scale of the problem, which I am happy to provide. I'd ask that the council raise this with Lime and take whatever action is appropriate, as this kind of incident cannot be allowed to keep happening unchecked.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Wyndham Road, Camberwell, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
